title: World editor button freezes on tap and never opens on iPhone
reproduction: Confirm Kelo Studio chrome appears immediately instead of a frozen World card.
Confirm the editor becomes interactive (tools/status, not only the loading shell).
Close/remove the Studio shell or reproduce the stale-session condition.
Open Create -> World again and confirm Studio remounts instead of black-screening.
expected: World opens, remains interactive, and can be reopened even after a stale Studio shell/session condition.
actual: Player iPhone 2026-09-14 22:03–22:04 still showed KELO STUDIO / Abriendo World Editor… then a fully black Safari tab (A3 / 5a52c6d). A4 / d6ff092 world-light still statically imported the Studio graph before chrome. A5 / world-chrome paints studio-live-shell first and chunks the controller graph. A6 / world-bridge is the current candidate: World first-hops a tiny paced bridge, iPhone prewarms runtime roots one-by-one with visible Cargando editor… n/N, core tools open first, rooms/paint/quick load after chrome.

research.summary: Four candidate directions exist. IndexedDB fail-open (A1) was insufficient. Curtain/stacking while awaiting ~80 modules (A2) failed LIVE. Early Hub destruction (A3) painted loading chrome then black-tabbed Safari. world-light (A4) delayed extras/overlay and dynamically imported studio-entry, but the live controller itself still statically imported the Studio graph, so iPhone still paid the 80-module cost before tools existed. world-chrome (A5) is the first candidate that actually paints .ks-status/tools from studio-live-shell.mjs before loading the controller graph. Target iPhone verification is still required. world-bridge (A6) adds a tiny first hop plus sequential iPhone prewarm and core-vs-build tool split. Target iPhone verification is still required.

evidence: 829ac7fbd5fc629b05ecf92489bab16b0292bce9 marked insufficient in the pre-v2 registry

hypotheses.theory: IndexedDB startup blocking is the primary cause of the World editor freeze.
hypotheses.why: A fail-open candidate targeted IndexedDB, but the player-facing failure persisted.
evidence_for: IndexedDB is in the boot path and was previously suspected
hypotheses.test_next: Do not spend another pass on IndexedDB alone unless a trace shows the current world-light boot waiting there before .ks-status.

hypotheses.theory: Hub stacking/visibility by itself is the root cause; painting a curtain and waiting for Studio should solve World open.
hypotheses.why: The 824a932 curtain/stacking candidate painted correctly but still failed while the Studio graph loaded.

hypotheses.theory: The large eager Studio import graph delays or prevents the interactive shell from mounting quickly enough on iPhone.
hypotheses.why: The failed 824a932 path requested about 80 Studio modules while the Hub stayed ABRIENDO and the interactive shell never attached within the observed window.
hypotheses.test_next: Verify world-chrome: .ks-top/.ks-status must exist before live-studio-controller starts fetching the remaining Studio graph on iPhone.

hypotheses.theory: Early overlay allocation at high devicePixelRatio contributes materially to Safari tab memory/resource failure after the loading shell paints.
hypotheses.why: The failed handoff reached loading chrome before the tab blacked out, and the previous registry specifically associated that path with the dpr=3 overlay plus the static graph.
hypotheses.test_next: On the current candidate, confirm the overlay is allocated only after chrome and capped at dpr<=1.5 on iPhone; if black-tab failure persists, compare a run with overlay creation disabled to isolate its contribution.

hypotheses.theory: The current world-light staged boot is sufficient to open an interactive Studio on the player's iPhone without black-screening.
hypotheses.why: Code inspection showed world-light still statically imported the Studio graph from the live controller before .ks-status existed, so it could not satisfy H3 even if extras/overlay were delayed.
hypotheses.test_next: Do not spend a real-iPhone pass on d6ff092 as-is; verify A5/world-chrome instead.

hypotheses.theory: Painting studio-live-shell chrome first, then dynamically importing the live controller graph in chunks, is sufficient for the player iPhone to reach interactive World tools without a black tab.
hypotheses.why: This is the first candidate that actually stages the graph after visible .ks-status/tools, which is the missing condition from A2/A3/A4.
hypotheses.test_next: Real iPhone Safari: Create -> World -> tools/.ks-status visible, then interactive, then close/reopen World.

ruled_out.theory: Hub stacking/visibility alone is the root cause.
ruled_out.reason: 824a932 fixed curtain/stacking behavior but still failed LIVE while the Studio graph loaded and the interactive shell did not attach.
evidence: F2

attempt_history.conclusion: Early Hub destruction exposes a different failure mode: loading chrome can paint, but the iPhone tab can die before interactive Studio is established. The handoff must preserve recovery while reducing boot/resource pressure.
attempt_history.do_not_repeat_without: A staged/lighter Studio graph and reduced early rendering allocation, plus a recovery path that keeps/restores the Hub if interactive mount fails.

attempt_history.goal: Stage World boot so interactive shell/status appears before extras and heavy rendering work, while preserving Hub recovery.

change.summary: Keep Hub until .ks-status; restore it if mount fails; load extras/palette after core; dynamically import studio-entry; paint shell before world import; cap iPhone overlay DPR at 1.5 and allocate after chrome.

validation.method: Exact Create -> World -> interactive tools/status -> close/reopen acceptance flow.

attempt_history.conclusion: This is the current candidate and must be attacked by target-device verification before another architecture rewrite is justified.

attempt_history.goal: Paint real Studio tools/status before importing the live controller graph, which A4 still loaded statically.

change.summary: Remove static Studio imports from the live controller. World paints studio-live-shell (.ks-top/.ks-status/tools) first, then dynamically loads the remaining graph in chunks. Pause updater during launch. Keep Hub recovery if hydrate fails.
